scope: underlying canonical budget/statistics/barangay data already in the repository

inventory.currentReportSourcePattern: Paragraph-level source IDs link to canonical BetterMakati pages; direct official-source links are not exposed in the article source schema.

classifications.factualStatus: core arithmetic is supported by the current canonical budget dataset
rationale: The article's 10.5% budget increase is specifically 2026 proposed appropriation versus the 2025 adopted plan.
The same canonical Projects & Budget page also shows a 2025 current-year estimate of ₱24.37B, above the ₱21.0B 2026 proposal.
The current headline and opening do not identify the adopted-plan baseline strongly enough, so a reader could interpret '2026 budget increase' as an increase over the city's latest 2025 estimate.
The MOOE concentration finding remains useful if the baseline is made explicit and the adopted-plan/current-estimate distinction is carried through the article.
classifications.migrationDirection: Retain the MOOE composition insight, but rewrite the headline, subheadline and article around the explicit 2025 adopted-plan comparison while also stating that the 2026 proposal is below the 2025 current-year estimate.

classifications.factualStatus: supported by the current DBM/BLGF-derived fiscal dataset
rationale: The 93.5% local-source share and concentration in business/property-related taxes form a coherent revenue-side finding.
As a standalone three-paragraph report it is thin and substantially overlaps the same 2025 fiscal source surface used by the social-services article.
It becomes more useful when paired with the spending-side evidence as one fiscal-profile synthesis rather than retained as a separate statistic article.
classifications.migrationDirection: Merge with 2025-social-services into one article whose single synthesis connects the source of 2025 receipts with the functional destination of 2025 spending, without implying causation between individual revenue streams and programs.

classifications.factualStatus: supported by the current DBM/BLGF-derived fiscal dataset
rationale: The 55.2% Social Services share is a valid functional-spending observation.
The current article is too close to a single table readout to justify a separate report beside the local-revenue article.
The category is broad, so the article should avoid implying program outcomes or service quality from expenditure classification alone.
classifications.migrationDirection: Merge with 2025-local-revenue into the same 2025 fiscal-profile article; retain the spending composition as the destination side of that one synthesis.

classifications.factualStatus: population counts and concentration arithmetic are supported by the current barangay/statistics datasets
rationale: The current article has a usable underlying point: resident population scale differs sharply across Makati's 23 barangays.
The headline 'three barangays contain 37.6%' is accurate but reads more like a statistical observation than a finished report synthesis.
The final paragraph moves toward service-demand implications even though daytime population, land use, facilities and service utilization are not part of the report's evidence.
classifications.migrationDirection: Rewrite around resident-population concentration and the order-of-magnitude difference in barangay scale. Keep service-demand claims out unless later evidence explicitly supports them.

reportsLanding.finding: The landing renders one report per card with headline, subheadline, date and Read more.
The BetterGov 'Related national data' box appears before the publication index and competes with the reports themselves.
All reports have equal card weight and the same date, so the landing has little editorial hierarchy.

reportArticle.finding: Paragraph-level [n] references already provide inline evidence links to canonical BetterMakati pages.
The current schema has paragraphs plus sources only; it cannot represent sections, charts/tables, typed canonical records, direct official sources or an explicit analysis/methodology distinction.
Articles are uniformly three paragraphs and can read like expanded stat cards rather than publication-grade reports.

homepage.finding: The homepage carousel already reuses the same canonical reports array as /reports and shows one report per card.
The homepage module should continue to consume canonical report objects after schema v2 so homepage and /reports cannot drift.

nextStep: W4-4b: define report schema v2 only. Do not rewrite or merge report content until W4-4c.
